claims.subject: tibalt

evidence.quote: What the gods don't know is that the real Valki has been imprisoned on Karfell by a cruel planeswalker, Tibalt, who has taken his place.
Tibalt wrapped Valki in magical chains and brought him to the coldest, most remote realm he could find: Karfell.

claims.summary: Tibalt imprisoned the real Valki on Karfell and took his place.

claims.subject: tibalt

evidence.quote: Tibalt wants to learn about the World Tree for some nefarious purpose and is trying to use Valki's identity to do so.

claims.summary: Tibalt uses Valki's identity as a disguise.

claims.subject: tibalt

evidence.quote: He had used it to unleash Koma on the Valkyries of Starnheim.

claims.summary: Tibalt used the Sword of the Realms to unleash Koma on the Valkyries.
claims.limitation: Episode 3 is narrated by Tibalt himself, who is unreliable; not independently confirmed in narration.

claims.subject: tyvar

evidence.quote: With a quick and practiced gesture, Tyvar knocked the sword from Tibalt's hands.
Tyvar pressed his brass blade to Tibalt's neck.

claims.summary: Tyvar disarmed and overpowered Tibalt in Immersturm.
claims.limitation: Tibalt is beaten in this fight, not killed.

claims.subject: kaya

evidence.quote: She beat a straight path for Tibalt, phasing through rock and fire and whatever else the devil threw her way; nimble as Tyvar was, she quickly pulled ahead of him.

claims.summary: Kaya pursued Tibalt in Immersturm.

claims.subject: demon_jarls

evidence.quote: Working together, for possibly the first time in history, the other jarls sealed Kardur hundreds of miles deep beneath the earth.

claims.summary: The other demon jarls sealed Kardur deep underground.

claims.subject: alrund

evidence.quote: When the Einir were defeated, Alrund took their seven surviving leaders and imprisoned them within seven great trees across their realm, which are now known as the Jaspera trees.

claims.summary: Alrund imprisoned the seven surviving Einir leaders inside the Jaspera trees.
claims.limitation: Strictly, the leaders of the Einir.

claims.subject: koll

evidence.quote: Koll was making a sword out of the stuff, a blade which could open paths between all the realms of Kaldheim.
Out of gratitude, Koll swore that he would forge the Tyrite into the finest blade the realms had ever seen as a gift for Halvar.

claims.summary: Koll forged the realm-opening Tyrite sword.
claims.limitation: Legends gives only Koll's oath; the forging is in Tibalt's narration (episode 3) and in dialogue (episode 5).

claims.subject: esika

evidence.quote: Esika makes the Cosmos Elixir that the gods consume to slow their aging and maintain their supernatural power.

claims.summary: Esika makes the Cosmos Elixir that the gods drink.

claims.subject: hurrik

evidence.quote: Just as the wolf was about to rip out Alrund's throat, Hurrik shot an arrow into its eye.

claims.summary: Hurrik saved Alrund from a Cosmos wolf.
claims.limitation: Told as a clan legend inside the guide.

claims.subject: varragoth

evidence.quote: Once in Bretagard, he quickly established himself as the leader of the Skelle raiders, who were all too happy to ally themselves with a demon.

claims.summary: Varragoth became the leader of the Skelle raiders.

claims.subject: toralf

evidence.quote: When Toralf asked his brother what troubled him, Valki threw down the harness in frustration.

claims.summary: Toralf and Valki are brothers.

claims.subject: vorinclex

evidence.quote: Why Vorinclex arrived in Kaldheim is currently unknown, but the purposes are certainly nefarious.
From the other side of the portal came a sound so unearthly and strange, she almost didn't recognize it as a voice: "Welcome back, Vorinclex.

claims.summary: Vorinclex of New Phyrexia came to Kaldheim, and in the epilogue a portal welcomes him back.
claims.limitation: Who greets him is not named here.

claims.subject: skoti

evidence.quote: Long ago, the Skoti had banished Koma from entering the realms, trapping him in the empty Cosmos.
In any case, the elves, who continue to worship Koma, believe that his banishment harms the World Tree.

claims.summary: The Skoti banished Koma to the Cosmos.
claims.limitation: The guide does not name who banished him; the Skoti come from Tibalt's narration in episode 3.

claims.subject: thura

evidence.quote: Thura Sail-Rend, she of the Beskir clan.

claims.summary: Thura Sail-Rend is of the Beskir clan.

claims.subject: arni_brokenbrow

evidence.quote: He's the new leader of the Tuskeri.
Arni Brokenbrow, they call him.

claims.summary: Arni Brokenbrow is the Tuskeri clan's new leader.
claims.limitation: The two lines are consecutive dialogue between the Valkyries; the name and the title are not in one sentence.

claims.subject: njala

evidence.quote: To her, a Valkyrie, no mortal seemed to last longer than a sunny afternoon

claims.summary: Njala is a Valkyrie who watches and judges the battle.
claims.limitation: 'Her' is Njala from the point-of-view narration.

claims.subject: njala

evidence.quote: She was trying to think of some point, some argument that would move her sister out of the way, when she saw it, over Alajn's shoulder.
muttered Njala to her sister.

claims.summary: The Valkyries Njala and Alajn are sisters.
claims.limitation: Sisterhood may be in the sense of fellow Valkyries; the text does not say blood relation.

claims.subject: egon

evidence.quote: In his place stood the very lord of Istfell himself, Egon, god of the dead

claims.summary: Egon, god of the dead, is the lord of Istfell.

claims.subject: inga_rune_eyes

evidence.quote: Inga, leader of the Omenseekers, was the first person Kaya had met on this plane

claims.summary: Inga Rune-Eyes leads the Omenseekers.

claims.subject: kaya

evidence.quote: Inga, leader of the Omenseekers, was the first person Kaya had met on this plane

claims.summary: Inga is the first person Kaya met on Kaldheim.

claims.subject: alrund

evidence.quote: In the bottom of the longship of Cosima, Kaya lay back and watched the night sky above drift by.
when Alrund had told her the ship

claims.summary: Alrund sends Kaya across the Cosmos on Cosima's longship.
claims.limitation: 'Aided' is an editorial reading of Alrund providing the ship.

claims.subject: niko_aris

evidence.quote: There was no sun or moon in Kaldheim, and its nights were growing longer.
glinted off Niko Aris's new breastplate and pauldrons

claims.summary: Niko Aris is on Kaldheim, in a longhall of warriors.

claims.subject: sarulf

evidence.quote: There was only one divine being that sent wolf children to his chosen, and that was Sarulf.

claims.summary: Sarulf sends a wolf child to Lathril, marking her as his chosen as she takes on godhood.
claims.limitation: The page shows the wolf with Lathril; the 'chosen' link is the narrator's inference.

remaining: Episodes 1-2 and the Kaya/Tibalt endgame in episode 5 are not graded
Koll's fate after Tibalt's attack is not graded (Tibalt narrates it, and later dialogue conflicts)
Elesh Norn's influence over Vorinclex is not graded
